think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: The patient presents with painless, refractory ulcerative plaques and satellite papules on his lower extremity that failed an extensive 3-week course of oral beta-lactamase-resistant antibiotic therapy. While chronic ulcerative plaques in endemic settings suggest cutaneous leishmaniasis, this case features prominent deep extension of the inflammatory process into subcutaneous adipose tissue causing septal and lobular panniculitis. This deep subcutaneous involvement mimics primary inflammatory or autoimmune panniculitides, even though the causative protozoal bodies are strictly localized to superficial dermal macrophages and completely absent within the inflamed panniculus.

2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission breakpoint occurs upon completion of the clinical and dermatologic evaluation of the left foot and ankle lesions following the failed antibiotic trial, strictly prior to skin punch biopsy, histopathological sectioning, and Giemsa staining.

3. Differential Distinctions:
- Refractory Bacterial Pyoderma / Ecthyma: Common bacterial etiology for crusted lower extremity ulcerations; excluded by complete lack of response to three weeks of oral ampicillin-cloxacillin and histological demonstration of chronic granulomatous inflammation.
- Primary Septal and Lobular Panniculitis (e.g., Erythema Induratum / Erythema Nodosum): Subcutaneous lobular and septal fat infiltration can suggest a primary panniculitis; excluded because the adipose inflammation was a sterile reactive phenomenon contiguous with a superficial dermal infection laden with amastigotes.
- Sporotrichosis / Deep Fungal Infection: Nodular and plaque-like lesions on the lower extremity; excluded by histopathological identification of Leishmania tropica bodies within macrophages on Giemsa stain.
case_prompt:
A 36-year-old male presents to the dermatology clinic with painless, non-healing nodular lesions on his left lower extremity of two months' duration. Prior to presentation, he completed an empiric three-week course of oral ampicillin-cloxacillin with no clinical response. His past medical and family history are otherwise unremarkable.

On physical examination, dermatological evaluation of the left lower extremity reveals a large ulcerative plaque on the dorsal aspect of the left foot, bordered by two satellite purple papules. In addition, multiple grouped, dusky erythematous, non-tender ulcerative nodules are present posterior to the lateral malleolus of the left leg. Systemic examination is otherwise unremarkable with no regional lymphadenopathy noted.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered initially as a conventional subacute bacterial skin and soft tissue infection. Ruled out by the lack of response to three weeks of systemic ampicillin-cloxacillin therapy and subsequent demonstration of protozoal amastigotes in the dermis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A 36-year-old male patient presented to our department with painless nodules on his left foot for a two-month duration for which he received a three-week course of systemic (ampicillin-cloxacillin) antibiotic without any improvement.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the prominent histopathological involvement of the subcutaneous adipose tissue showing lobular and septal inflammatory changes. Ruled out as the panniculitis was a secondary reactive phenomenon to a superficial dermal infection, and no protozoal bodies were present in the panniculus itself.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: These changes even involved the panniculus causing septal and lobular panniculitis (Figure 1(c)). The Leishmania tropica (LT) bodies were seen in numerous numbers inside the macrophages of superficial dermis in sections stained with H&E and Gimesa. Some of them were extracellular. These bodies were distributed in the dermis in a form of foci. They were absent in the lesions of panniculitis.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis was confirmed by skin biopsy of the ulcerative plaque showing a dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with early granulomas and numerous Leishmania tropica (LT) bodies within superficial dermal macrophages on H&E and Giemsa staining.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The Leishmania tropica (LT) bodies were seen in numerous numbers inside the macrophages of superficial dermis in sections stained with H&E and Gimesa. Some of them were extracellular. These bodies were distributed in the dermis in a form of foci.

editor_comments: Strict adherence to admission breakpoint. Presentation captures chronic painless foot ulcers and satellite nodules prior to biopsy. Differentials and diagnostic pivot are supported by exact verbatim quotes.
